transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-02
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marcus (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Daniel (CTO - Zenith), Priya (Head of MLOps), Carlos (Security), Maya (Network)

Summary: quick discovery about private VPC deployment, network constraints, SOC2 concerns, and next steps.

[00:00] Aisha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, appreciate you making time. Quick intro from our side - I'm Aisha, I'm the AE, um Marcus and Jordan are our SEs.
[00:12] Daniel: Thanks. I'm Daniel, CTO at Zenith. We run a bunch of analytics pipelines and are evaluating Redwood for inference hosting, specifically private VPC for compliance.
[00:22] Priya: Hi, Priya here. Leading MLOps. Main ask is we need private endpoints and no public egress for model payloads and logs.
[00:30] Carlos: Carlos from Security - SOC2 and key management, also audit logs retention questions.
[00:36] Marcus: Great, high level we support three deployment modes - Hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private, which is what we'll talk about. For Private we can do a customer VPC peering or private endpoints, depending on cloud and needs.
[00:48] Maya: Quick clarification: do you require cross-account peering or a managed endpoint inside our VPC?
[00:54] Jordan: We support both patterns. On AWS we often do VPC peering or PrivateLink (AWS NLB + interface endpoints) depending on whether you want control plane to be in your account or if you want us to manage the control plane but keep data path private.
[01:10] Daniel: Our preference is that traffic never traverses the public internet; ideally private within our account. Also regions matter — our EU data must stay in eu-west-1.
[01:20] Marcus: Noted. We can pin the control plane region and ensure model serving happens in selected region. There are some caveats around available instance types per region though.
[01:30] Priya: What about VPC CIDR overlap? Our network team is strict — we have a lot of legacy ranges.
[01:36] Maya: yes, we have 10.0.0.0/8 chunks in use; peering may be tricky. We prefer to use PrivateLink or Transit Gateway to avoid CIDR overlap.
[01:46] Jordan: Right, Transit Gateway can be used as well. If there's CIDR overlap, we typically recommend using an intermediary (transit gateway) or customer-managed NAT/proxies. There's also option for an ingress NLB in our account accepting encrypted traffic.
[02:05] Carlos: How do you handle KMS? Keys must be in our control for encryption at rest.
[02:12] Marcus: We integrate with customer KMS/HSM for Private deployments — you can bring your own key. For Hosted we have Redwood-managed KMS, but for Private we support your KMS so keys never leave your control.
[02:24] Daniel: Great. And audit logging — we need immutable logs for 1 year and the ability to export to our SIEM.
[02:31] Jordan: We provide audit logs and can stream them to customer S3 or to CloudWatch/Stackdriver. For Private we can route logs into your account so they never traverse our telemetry pipeline.
[02:42] Priya: Any differences in latency/cost between Private and Dedicated? We care about 99th percentile latency inferences under 120ms for our use-case.
[02:50] Marcus: There's tradeoffs. Dedicated reserved pools in your tenancy give most predictable latency and throughput. Private with peering or PrivateLink adds a bit of network hop depending on setup, but with colocated GPUs in the same AZ you can still meet 100-120ms p99. Hosted might have multi-tenant variance.
[03:10] Daniel: Can you do region-local model variants? We need eu-only models for GDPR reasons.
[03:16] Marcus: Yes, you can pin model versions and variants to regions. We'll ensure weights and caches remain in-region for Private deployments.
[03:24] Maya: How do you handle egress? Our compliance forbids egress to unapproved IP ranges — we need to know all IPs Redwood uses for outbound traffic if any.
[03:35] Jordan: For Private, we minimize outbound. If we need to reach external registries for model pulls during onboarding, that's done through your registry or we can push images into your account. We'll provide a documented IP range list for required control plane endpoints, but for data plane we aim to keep it inside your VPC.
[03:50] Carlos: Are there any third-party dependencies that could leak metadata?
[03:54] Marcus: We try to avoid third-party callouts for Private. Any monitoring/observability can be configured to route into your monitoring stack. We'll share our SOC2/ISO docs that describe data handling.
[04:05] Daniel: Ok let's go deeper on networking - Maya, can you cover constraints?
[04:09] Maya: Sure. We prefer no peering that requires changing route tables broadly; we also can't accept overlapping CIDRs. Preferred options: interface endpoints (PrivateLink), or creating a dedicated account with our transit gateway for peering. Also need support for multi-AZ redundancy.
[04:24] Jordan: That matches our recommendations. For PrivateLink we create an NLB in the provider account pointing to the serving fleet; customer creates interface endpoints in their VPC. That avoids CIDR overlap and is cross-account.
[04:36] Maya: How is authentication handled over PrivateLink?
[04:39] Jordan: Typically mTLS or mutual TLS plus token auth. We also support SAML/OIDC for admin console access. For data plane RPCs we use signed tokens and you can enforce IP restriction via endpoint policies.
[04:51] Priya: For canary/rollouts we need to be able to route a percentage of traffic to new model versions — does that work inside Private?
[04:57] Marcus: Yes, rollouts are supported. Policy and routing are consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. You can do canary by route or model variant.
[05:06] Daniel: You mentioned model pulls earlier — how long would onboarding take for our models and data if we want a private deployment?
[05:12] Marcus: Typical timeline: network setup and security review 1-2 weeks, infra provisioning and cluster spin up 1 week, model onboarding and validation 1-2 weeks depending on size. So roughly 3-5 weeks end-to-end for a standard private deployment.
[05:26] Priya: Are there minimums for Dedicated nodes or GPU types?
[05:30] Marcus: For Dedicated we have minimum commit sizes — usually starts at 3 GPUs for a cluster to ensure redundancy. GPU type depends on region — we'll call out exact SKUs per region in the follow-up.
[05:40] Maya: Are you able to run inside Azure as well or only AWS?
[05:44] Jordan: We support AWS, GCP, and Azure for Private deployments; availability per region varies. We'll include region-level compatibility matrix.
[05:53] Carlos: For compliance we need RBAC and SSO for console access and audit logs for admin actions.
[05:59] Marcus: We support SAML SSO, SCIM for provisioning, RBAC, and we can push admin audit logs to your audit account.
[06:07] Daniel: If we do peering, how are IPs allocated? We can't change our CIDRs easily — we might need you to support NAT or egress through our NAT gateway.
[06:16] Jordan: If CIDR overlap exists we typically use PrivateLink or we assign provider-side IPs in a non-overlapping range and route through transit gateway. There's tradeoffs around hairpinning and asymmetry; we'll document pros/cons.
[06:29] Priya: Any constraints on TLS termination? We require TLS termination inside our environment.
[06:33] Marcus: Fine — we can pass TLS through to your NLB or terminate in your ingress. Mutual TLS is supported.
[06:39] Maya: Also need to understand how autoscaling triggers affect peering — if you auto-scale into new subnets, will routes be updated automatically?
[06:46] Jordan: Autoscaling within the cluster is handled by our orchestration, and route propagation via transit gateway or endpoint registration is part of the setup. We'll document the behavior.
[06:55] Daniel: Let's talk SLOs — we need p50/p95/p99 targets and observability hooks.
[06:59] Marcus: Our console provides per-route token-level latency, per-model dashboards, tracing hooks. For performance SLOs we'll work with you on load profiles. We'll include recommended batch sizes and KV cache settings to hit p99 targets with minimum cost.
[07:13] Priya: On the caching comment, does KV cache persist across restarts? We want warm starts for commonly used prompts.
[07:18] Jordan: Yes, KV cache is persisted in the serving layer for Private deployments; cache policies can be tuned. Cache persistence across node churn depends on your storage choices; we can pin local SSDs or use network-backed cache depending on latency needs.
[07:33] Maya: For network egress audit, we need a list of outbounds for OS and agent updates.
[07:38] Marcus: We'll provide a comprehensive list: control-plane IPs, registries for pulls, and update servers. We can also vendor images into your registry to avoid outbound pulls.
[07:48] Daniel: How is billing handled for Private? Is usage metered or flat commit?
[07:52] Aisha: Usually Private is licensed as enterprise with a platform fee plus infra charges. Dedicated reserved can be committed monthly/annually. We'll send a pricing estimate for a 3-node config.
[08:01] Priya: Any limits on models? We run Llama-family and a few custom large models.
[08:06] Marcus: We support a wide catalog, including open Llama variants; for very custom models we'll do validation and quantization recommendations. We'll advise on quantization profiles for cost/perf.
[08:18] Maya: For egress to SIEM, do you push logs or can we pull?
[08:22] Jordan: Both. We can stream logs to your account or provide log export endpoints.
[08:27] Daniel: Let's surface risks — what are common blockers customers hit?
[08:31] Marcus: Commonly CIDR overlap, procurement timelines for enterprise contracts, and region-specific GPU availability. Also internal security reviews around KMS and audit logging can add time.
[08:43] Priya: For the security review, can you share an architecture diagram and a threat model doc?
[08:48] Aisha: Yes — we'll attach the standard private deployment architecture, threat model, and our security pack.
[08:55] Maya: For our internal change freeze windows, we might only open new peering on certain dates — timeline needs to account for that.
[08:61] Jordan: (laugh) small slip on time there 08:61 but noted — we'll coordinate timelines.
[09:05] Daniel: ok um, one more — what's your approach to secrets (API keys, model weights)? We can't expose secrets to operator teams.
[09:13] Marcus: Secrets are stored in customer KMS for Private. Access controls are via RBAC and audit logged. We can also integrate with HSMs.
[09:22] Priya: For training vs serving, we only care about inference here, right?
[09:26] Marcus: Correct, this is inference serving only. Training is out-of-scope.
[09:29] Daniel: Can you do a staged pilot in our dev account first?
[09:33] Aisha: Yes, many customers run a dev pilot, we recommend starting with a small cluster and a defined eval set. We'll run some synthetic load tests and a short quality/regression eval.
[09:43] Marcus: We'll include benchmark scripts and a sample workload to reproduce p99 latency under typical token lengths.
[09:49] Maya: For region eu-west-1, any capacity constraints currently?
[09:53] Jordan: There's some demand but we can provision — we will confirm exact GPU SKUs and availability in the follow-up.
[09:58] Priya: For model artifacts, we prefer artifact storage in our account. Can you pull from S3/GCS/Azure storage?
[10:04] Jordan: Yes — we can pull from your artifact storage via a short-lived signed URL or you can push images into a repo in your account.
[10:12] Daniel: Ok sounds good. Let's recap next steps.
[10:16] Aisha: Quick recap: we'll send security docs, network checklist, region compatibility, and a pricing estimate. Marcus will prepare benchmark plan. We should schedule a networking deep-dive with Maya and your infra folks next week.
[10:27] Daniel: Works for us. Priya will share CIDR ranges and preferred regions.
[10:31] Priya: Yep will do.
[10:33] Carlos: We'll review SOC2 docs once you send them.
[10:36] Aisha: Great. Any final Qs?
[10:38] Daniel: Not from me.
[10:40] Marcus: One last note — for fallback we can configure automatic model variant fallback to smaller quantized models if capacity is constrained, which can reduce latency but we should test for quality.
[10:51] Priya: Good to know.
[10:54] Aisha: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and propose times for the deep-dive.
[10:58] Daniel: Thanks all.

End meeting.

Notes on transcription and artifacts:
- Some timestamps are approximate; transcription had minor speaker overlaps and occasional mis-hear of product names (e.g., "Redwood Inferense" transcribed once).
- Shared artifacts to attach: private-deploy-arch.pdf (link to shared drive), security-pack.zip (SOC2/ISO), region-capacity-matrix.xlsx (to be attached by Redwood).
